shapes.name: array_length
shapes.reason: An array's own length, not a caller-supplied number. A JS array cannot be longer than the safe-integer range, so the read has nothing to saturate; the budget on that length is the array-length guard's, which the shared wasmArrayLength applies.

readers.reason: An enum resolver for the pan-law ordinal, taking the string and numeric spellings together. The numeric path requires a finite, integral value inside the enum's bounds before the cast, so a saturated, negative, fractional or non-finite ordinal is refused by name; the two legal ordinals pan differently, which is what makes those refusals a measurement rather than an unread field.

Reads through double rather than narrowing, so no integer cast happens here and the inline-narrowing population does not see it. It is a second numeric reader outside the shared family all the same. Its own range check is the mechanism: a value outside [0, max] or a fractional one is refused naming the field, and a non-finite one is refused by the shared requireNumberProperty it reads through.

The floating-point sibling of integerField, under the same standing. It type-checks and refuses a non-finite value through the shared requireNumberProperty and returns the double unnarrowed; the float narrowing is the caller's, and it can only overflow for values already far outside the field's physical domain, where the representable neighbours render identically.

An enum resolver for the sample loop mode, accepting the SoundFont numeric value and the name spellings. The numeric path is integerField's, so the ordinal is refused outside [0, 3] and for a fractional or non-finite value; an unknown name is refused naming the accepted set.

An enum resolver, not a size reader: the ordinal it returns is range-checked by the C ABI against the curve enum's bounds. Recorded here rather than folded into the shared family because the reader shape is incidental -- it exists to accept both the string and the numeric spelling of one enum.

Delegates every element's narrowing to the shared checkedWordFromVal and the array's length to the shared wasmArrayLength, so the conversion contract is single-sourced. What is local is the message's own domain: a UMP carries one to four words, which only the two raw-UMP push entry points ask.

Delegates the narrowing to the shared optionalDomainValue against the C ABI's own sample-bank byte domain, so the conversion contract is single-sourced. What is local is only the absent-key spelling: an omitted descriptor byte maps to the C zero that selects the library default.

Returns the array's own length through the shared wasmArrayLength after checking each element's shape; it narrows no caller-supplied number, and every numeric field is read later by the shared readers under the indexed subject.

shapes.name: sixty_four_bit

mechanism.note: The shipped embind glue, where the 64-bit toWireType lives. It is the build's output and no committed file carries it, so the citation is marked built: an absent dist is not a failure, a dist whose glue no longer reads this way is. The other half of the claim -- that this population is the 64-bit one at all -- is derived from the declared types rather than cited.

shapes.reason: A 64-bit parameter is registered through __embind_register_bigint, not through the integer path: its toWireType converts a JS number with BigInt(value), which throws on a fractional and on a non-finite one, and no number below 2^63 has anything to wrap into. The blessing belongs to the width, not to the field: this pattern selects on the declared type alone, so the population is every 64-bit parameter -- timeline positions and page ordinals alike -- and naming it after one of those meanings would claim a check nothing performs. The one residue is a request past 2^63, where the BigInt-to-i64 conversion truncates; it is integral, so it cannot arrive by the fractional truncation these records exist for, and no field of any meaning here addresses a domain that large.

passthroughs.name: hz

mechanism.contains: saturates to an infinity the same way the C conversion does

passthroughs.reason: A total function over the whole real line, and documented as one on the surface a consumer reads. Refusing a saturated value here would make the mel mapping disagree with the C ABI, with Node and with the reference implementation it mirrors, for a conversion that has no rejecting branch to reach.

mechanism.contains: Slaney mel scale to frequency in Hz. Total over the same domain as

passthroughs.reason: The inverse of hzToMel under the same contract: the pair has to accept the same domain or a round trip stops being one.

passthroughs.name: hz
passthroughs.reason: Non-finite is meaningful input here rather than a caller error: an unvoiced frame of a pitch track is NaN, and mapping a whole track through this is the documented use. A checked reader refuses NaN, so routing it would reject the convention's own spelling.

passthroughs.name: midi

mechanism.contains: `-Infinity` bottoms out at 0 rather than propagating its sign

passthroughs.reason: The inverse of hzToMidi, and its documented behaviour is specifically about what it does with an infinity -- a value it must therefore be able to receive.

passthroughs.name: hz

mechanism.contains: past the representable MIDI range, and non-finite alike

passthroughs.reason: The core refuses every frequency with no note, non-finite included, with a coded InvalidParameter, so a saturated value is refused there exactly as any other unnameable one. A checked reader ahead of it would only duplicate that refusal under a different message.
